newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest spot power down, Southwest higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest spot power down, Southwest higher.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Northwest were weaker, while Southwest prices were marginally higher after news of a delay in restarting a California nuclear power plant, market sources said Thursday.
The differential between the regions was "almost enough to buy power in the Northwest and ship it down south," but transmission capacity was unavailable, said one trader.
Demand throughout the region was described as lackluster amid unseasonally mild weather conditions.
Power supplies in general were seen as plentiful, with abundant hydropower volumes offsetting any concerns related to the usual short-term outages at thermal generation plants.

But the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California was not expected to restart until early March after the discovery of a generator tube leak on Wednesday, a Southern California Edison Co spokesman said.
The unit was shut Nov 30 for a scheduled refueling outage, which had already been extended to the end of February so that tube repairs could be carried out.
Meanwhile, the 1,221 MW unit 3 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant near Wintersburg, Ariz., was expected to be completely off-line by midnight on Friday for scheduled refueling.

In the Northwest, where low-cost hydropower continues to set the market, the 1,158 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear unit in Washington will run at 55 percent capacity until Bonneville Power Administration requests otherwise.
Northwest temperatures were expected to be near normal Thursday, but were called to climb to five to 10 degrees F above normal Friday through Tuesday.
The Southwest was expected to see temperatures of six to 12 degrees above normal through early next week.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Friday was quoted at $9.50-10.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from $10.00-11.00 for Thursday.
Firm, off-peak COB quotes for Friday were at $6.50-7.00.
Firm, peak electricity at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) for Friday was slightly lower at $8.50-9.50.
Off-peak Mid-C for day-ahead delivery was quoted at $5.50-6.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was quoted at $13.00-14.00, compared with $12.25-13.00 for Thursday.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $12.75-13.75, while off-peak was at $6.50-7.50.
